input.quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor. Customer owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective termination date, and Vendor shall promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the period after that date. Vendor has no corresponding convenience-termination right during a committed term.
input.rationale: Section 9.4 satisfies every preferred element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience on thirty days' written notice, Vendor must promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the post-termination period, and Vendor is expressly denied a corresponding convenience right during a committed term. No early-termination fee or penalty attaches, and a document-wide review of the termination provisions (§§ 9.1–9.5, 8.2–8.3, 27.3, 24.4) shows no Vendor right to terminate without cause; § 8.2 non-renewal is Customer-side only and in any event belongs under RENEWAL. The one tension is § 2.1's three-year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights", which cuts against the § 9.4 exit economics; that is the minimum-commitment bargain and is addressed under MINCOMMIT rather than flagged twice here. No redline proposed.
